source_or_gap: The book specified runtime, typed work, delegation, and deployment boundaries but lacked a chapter owning the progression of AI work surfaces from conversational answer and inline suggestion through repository harness, project steward, role, team, organization, and inter-organizational network.
chapter_action_policy: Use Copilot, Augment, Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, and Oh My Pi as dated coding-harness landmarks; use Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, and elizaOS as freestanding-runtime landmarks; compare custody and authority dimensions rather than ranking products. Retain each project's existing mechanism-owner mappings.
merge_or_split_policy: Keep separate source records because the products have different maintainers, surfaces, and evidentiary boundaries. Create one comparative architecture chapter, not one chapter per product, and preserve the existing mechanism owners.
boundary_decision_rationale: No existing chapter owns the transfer of work surface itself: what context, persistence, tools, state, authority, review, and accountability move as AI expands from an answer to a project, role, team, organization, or network. Runtime Adapters owns effects; Human-AI Organizations owns delegation; Deployment Transition owns social distribution. The new chapter owns the transition model and its future branches.
external_literature_need: track stable releases or archival design papers if the projects publish them
compare shared Agent Skills and ACP standards against their canonical specifications
find independent evaluations of security, reliability, procedural learning, and long-horizon operation
proof_or_test_backlog: build a version-pinned cross-runtime turn-spine fixture joining request, run, session, authority, effect, observation, and terminal disposition
test that external harness resume identifiers cannot substitute for local session or authority identity
test skill proposal hash binding, stale-target rejection, rollback custody, quarantine, and independent regression gates
compare sandbox location, tool availability policy, approval, and elevated execution as independent controls
evidence_transition_precondition: freeze the exact source revision, claim atom, workload, consumer, and comparison baseline
execute or independently inspect the relevant implementation path
retain configuration, failures, costs, limitations, and unresolved residuals
required_before_drafting: completed: official repository identity and revision check
completed: canonical architecture, runtime, memory, skill, security, session, ACP, and scenario documentation review
completed: nine source notes and inventory records
completed: comparative chapter and existing-owner crosswalk
promotion_blockers: the projects were inspected but not run in this repository
no reported behavior or test result was independently reproduced
no common workload, configuration, or version-pinned baseline has been executed
next_action: Keep support unchanged and schedule the version-pinned cross-runtime identity, policy-separation, and procedure-promotion fixtures only when they outrank the active roadmap's current empirical and proof work.
non_claims: does not establish that any reviewed project is safe, correct, state of the art, AGI, or ASI
does not claim feature parity or architectural equivalence
does not reproduce any repository test, benchmark, or production result
creates a comparative chapter at argument support and does not promote support
